answer: Sybil resistance binds each identity to bonded collateral and aggregates proof of coordinated equivocation: if k identities sign conflicting claims in concert, the slashing charge scales as O(k²), rather than linearly. Upon detection, an additional capital-loss multiplier grows exponentially with k across linked escrows, making a large swarm far more costly than its apparent per-identity stake suggests. Labels such as yarrow, oasis, or marble do not conceal common control or alter the penalty.
